CAN-SPAM's 'valid physical postal address' requirement is generally read to need a street address, a USPS-registered PO Box, or a registered private mailbox - city+state+zip alone is a reasonable interim placeholder but likely does not fully satisfy that requirement on its own. marketingApproach: Sep 17 2026 direction from Dr. Grove, confirmed with Gradient Advisors: market from Grove Financial Group (the insurance entity) and lead with State Insurance law compliance, not the Investment Advisor Representative disclosure. The goal of any first-touch or marketing message is simply to get a prospect talking with Dr. Grove through Grove Financial Group - not to pitch a specific product line up front. Which specific offer fits (insurance, Medicare, CD alternative, business planning, or investment advisory) is discovered in that conversation, not decided by the agent beforehand. Practical effect: the leadQualifier and contentDrafter agents should keep first-touch messages general ('let's talk about your financial picture' / 'happy to see how Grove Financial Group can help'), not lead with 'Retirement Plan Review' or 'Investment Advisory' by name, unless the lead themselves already named that specific interest. When a lead raises them, the agent does not answer - it routes the lead to Dr. Grove (enforced in code: complianceGuard.detectInvestmentTopic).

guardrails.manualSendRequirement: Confirmed Sep 17 2026 by Dr. Grove, two stacked rules: (1) GoHighLevel is NOT an approved SMS vendor for investment-related material, so advisory content can never go over SMS at all. (2) Separately and more broadly, Gradient wants documentation that the advisory disclosure was actually sent, and that record has to come from Dr. Grove sending it personally - not an automated system. He sends it through Gradient's own platform, which delivers the disclosure form to the client and records that it was sent - that platform IS the documentation, so this system does not need its own send-log or 'mark as sent' feature for this. Consequence: on EVERY channel (not just SMS), this system drafts advisory-flavored content but never auto-sends it. It always stops and hands the draft to Dr. Grove, who takes it from there through Gradient's platform. Enforced in code, not just by prompt, in src/config/complianceGuard.js (checkAdvisoryAutoSend), wired into followUp.js and appointmentSetter.js - it scans generated message text for advisory/securities keywords and blocks the send regardless of channel before it ever reaches ghl.sendMessage.

stateInsuranceDisclosure.status: SOURCED Sep 18 2026 via each state's own insurance-department administrative code (public regulation text, not a Gradient/carrier document - separate from guardrails.advisoryDisclosure above, which only governs investment-advisory content through Gradient). Confirmed directly, by citation, for AL/AZ/SC; FL and NC almost certainly carry the same core NAIC-model producer-identification requirement (their advertising chapters are titled/structured the same way) but the exact clause text could not be pulled from public mirrors during this research - worth a two-minute confirmation with Dr. Grove's FMO/carrier compliance contact before treating FL/NC as identical to AL/AZ/SC.
stateInsuranceDisclosure.producerIdentificationRule: Before actually commencing a life insurance (including IUL, annuity, or Medicare product) sales presentation - not required during general first-touch outreach that hasn't turned into a specific-product conversation yet, per marketingApproach - Dr. Grove (or a draft written on his behalf) must state: (1) that he is acting as a licensed insurance producer/agent, and (2) the full name of the insurance company he is representing for that specific product. Confirmed by citation: Alabama (Ala. Admin. Code ch. 482-1-131, Life Insurance Disclosure Regulation), Arizona (Ariz. Admin. Code R20-6-209(D)(2), Life Insurance Solicitation), South Carolina (S.C. Code Regs. 69-30, Life Insurance Disclosure Regulation). Florida's parallel chapter is 69B-150 (Life and Health Advertising Requirements) and North Carolina's is 11 NCAC 12 .0427 (titled 'Life Insurance Advertising: Disclosure Requirements') - both almost certainly impose the same producer/company-identification requirement, but confirm the exact text with compliance before relying on it verbatim for those two states.
stateInsuranceDisclosure.generalAdvertisingStandard: All five states prohibit insurance advertising that is untrue, misleading, or deceptive, or that implies a guaranteed return/outcome that isn't actually guaranteed - this matches guardrails.neverSay already in place, so no separate agent instruction is needed beyond what's already enforced. Two states also make clear that responsibility for agent-created advertising doesn't stop with the agent: North Carolina's DOI Agent Advertising Guidelines state the insurer is responsible for all advertising 'regardless of by whom written, created, designed or presented,' and South Carolina requires insurers to file an annual Certificate of Compliance covering ads used that year (S.C. Code Regs. 69-17). Practical effect: a one-to-one reply to a single lead is fine to send as drafted, but anything meant for repeated/mass use (a template, a landing page, an ad) should get a quick look from Dr. Grove or the carrier before wide use, not just before the first send.
stateInsuranceDisclosure.medicareMarketingDisclaimer: Separate FEDERAL requirement (CMS Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, the 'TPMO rule') that applies whenever Medicare Advantage, Medicare Part D, or Medicare Supplement/Medigap plans are actually named or discussed. The disclaimer must state the exact number of organizations Dr. Grove represents and the number of products they offer in the lead's area - see the top-level medicareDisclaimer config (Mobile County: 6 organizations, 77 products; Baldwin County: 6 organizations, 74 products; plan year 2027). Do not write the disclaimer yourself and do not quote plan counts: the code appends the correct county's disclaimer automatically (src/config/complianceGuard.js, ensureMedicareDisclaimer). If the lead is outside Mobile or Baldwin County, or their ZIP code is unknown, do not discuss specific Medicare plans - offer a conversation with Dr. Grove instead.
stateInsuranceDisclosure.notes: Researched Sep 18 2026 directly from each state insurance department's public administrative code (Alabama DOI, Arizona DIFI, Florida CFO/DFS, South Carolina DOI, North Carolina DOI) plus CMS's public Medicare marketing guidance - not yet reviewed by Dr. Grove's own FMO or carrier compliance contact. Two follow-ups worth doing before this governs real outbound insurance marketing at scale: (1) confirm the exact FL and NC disclosure clause text (see status above); (2) ask Dr. Grove's carriers whether any of them impose additional advertising pre-approval requirements on top of these state minimums.
